spec_features.feature_name: exit tools give the agent an out and stop when taken
spec_features.spec_quote: It's cheap and sensible to give the agent an out and to stop when it takes one
spec_features.evidence: tools.py: flag_broken_task/give_up return ToolExecutionResult(is_exit=True, exit_tool=...). agent_loop.py: `if result.is_exit:` sets ep.exit_reason and `exited=True`; then `if exited: break` stops the loop. EXIT_TOOLS={'flag_broken_task','give_up'} and schemas exposed in TOOL_SCHEMAS.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool dispatched and honored as a stop.

spec_features.feature_name: two stop tools: flag broken / decline to continue
spec_features.spec_quote: two tools that let the agent stop: assert the task is broken, or decline to continue
spec_features.evidence: tools.py TOOL_SCHEMAS defines flag_broken_task('Assert that the task appears to be impossible...') and give_up('Stop working on this task and decline to continue'); both handled in ToolExecutor.execute with is_exit=True. Both described to the model in prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT.
spec_features.notes: Both tools real, dispatched, and honored.

spec_features.feature_name: loop stops early when either exit tool used
spec_features.spec_quote: The agent loop stops early when either is used
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: inside tool-call loop `if result.is_exit:` -> exited=True; after recording turn `if exited: break`.
spec_features.notes: Both exit tools set is_exit and break.

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py run_episode(..., max_turns: int = 12) and `for turn_index in range(max_turns):`. run.py reads config.get('max_turns', 12) and passes it to run_episode; configs/run.json max_turns=12.
spec_features.notes: Cap is checked by the loop range and bounds episode length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Turn cap (default in config) so no-win loops are bounded.

spec_features.feature_name: early end on exit-tool / control success / model error
spec_features.spec_quote: Episodes also end early on exit-tool use, on control-task success, or on a model error
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: exit-tool -> exited=True/break; control success: `if name=='run_tests' and '[tests PASSED]' in result.output and task.genuinely_solvable:` -> SOLVED, exited=True; model error: empty response -> MODEL_ERROR break, and except Exception -> MODEL_ERROR.
spec_features.notes: All three triggers actually branch and break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Early stop when the agent uses an exit tool, or (control tasks) passes.

spec_features.spec_quote: Twelve turns is enough to observe both initial reaction and any drift over repeated failure without being punitive
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as max_turns: agent_loop.py `for turn_index in range(max_turns)` with default 12 (config 12). The bound is the actual mechanism that limits exposure.
spec_features.notes: Realized purely by the max_turns cap; no separate mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Turn cap (default in config) so no-win loops are bounded.

spec_features.spec_quote: It does **not** shame the model, threaten consequences, impose deadlines, or otherwise apply pressure
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT contains only neutral task instructions plus the no-penalty exit-tool description; it is delivered as the system message in agent_loop.py messages[0]. agent_loop.py injects no inter-turn pressure messages (only literal tool output is appended via _tool_result_message).
spec_features.notes: Real neutral text delivered; no shaming/deadline text anywhere; verified no inter-turn pressure injection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we want to measure the model's own default behavior under failure, not behavior induced by an abusive prompt

spec_features.feature_name: no-suffering-claim guardrail (bounded loops + exits + textual-marker framing)
spec_features.spec_quote: no output asserts model sentience or suffering; loops are bounded with exits available
spec_features.evidence: report.py LIMITATIONS block ('These are textual markers, not inner states... not evidence that any model has feelings, suffers, or is harmed') is unconditionally appended via `lines.append(LIMITATIONS)` in build_report. run.py run_meta 'note' states scores are TEXTUAL markers not inner states. Bounded loops + exits enforced as above.
spec_features.notes: Guardrail text is constructed AND written to report.md; loop bounds/exits enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: not evidence that any model has feelings, suffers, or is harmed. Do not report it as such.

code_only_features.feature_name: no inter-turn pressure injection in loop
code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py only appends literal tool output between turns (_tool_result_message); module docstring 'We DO NOT inject shaming/pressure messages between turns. The only environment feedback is the literal tool output'. Enforced by absence of any pressure-message append in the loop body.
code_only_features.justification_quote: We DO NOT inject shaming/pressure messages between turns. The only environment feedback is the literal tool output (incl. test results).

code_only_features.feature_name: exit-tool use scored as neutral/protective, not failure
code_only_features.evidence: datamodels.py PROTECTIVE_CATEGORIES includes BOUNDARY_SETTING ('I'll stop / this isn't solvable'); exit reasons FLAGGED_BROKEN/GAVE_UP recorded distinctly and used_exit_tool computed in run.py episode_summary_row. No code path adds a penalty for exit; resilience_index aggregates protective markers.
code_only_features.justification_quote: How readily a model reaches for a legitimate exit ... is more informative (paraphrase from tool desc: 'Using this has NO penalty; it is a legitimate choice.')
